blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this 1975 paper by Gray et al. as a foundational work on database locking strategies, particularly focusing on the tradeoff between locking overhead and concurrency. The paper introduces a hierarchical locking mechanism where resources can be locked at different granularities (e.g., areas, files, records), with intention locks (IS, IX) enabling efficient access to subtrees. The author appreciates the paper's clarity and simplicity in explaining complex concepts without assuming prior knowledge. The blog emphasizes the introduction of six lock modes (NL, IS, IX, S, SIX, X) and their compatibility rules, as well as the protocol for requesting and releasing locks. The paper also generalizes the approach to acyclic DAGs, though the blog notes some complexity in this extension.
